caption: A boy takes a short run-up on a field, leaps forward off one foot, and after landing on both feet takes a few stumbling steps forward before he stops.

sa.check: A boy takes a run-up on a field.
He leaps forward off one foot.
He takes a few stumbling steps forward and comes to a stop.
The run-up is short rather than a long approach.
The run-up comes first, then the leap, then the landing, then the steps.

pc.expect: He rises after the take-off, then comes down, falling quicker the nearer he gets to the ground.
pc.fail: He keeps rising until he leaves the frame; or he holds still at the top of the leap; or he drops straight down from the take-off point without ever rising.

pc.expect: His flight carries him forward from where he took off, and the stumbling steps continue that way from the moment he lands.
pc.fail: He comes down behind where he took off, having travelled backward through the air; or he stumbles backward or sideways after landing; or he stops dead on the spot as his feet touch down.

pc.expect: Once in the air he keeps the course the leap gave him; he is carried along the ground only while his feet are driving him.
pc.fail: He changes direction in mid-air; or he gathers speed in mid-air; or he slides on across the grass with his feet planted and still.

pc.expect: The grass flattens where he drives off and where he lands, and springs back or stays pressed.
pc.fail: Torn-up grass rises away and hangs in the air; or the ground ripples like water under his feet; or the turf stays untouched where he plainly drove off it.
pc.precondition: Grass or loose ground is visibly disturbed by his feet.

pc.expect: One boy keeps his limbs, his number and his shape, and he stays above the ground.
pc.fail: A limb stretches, detaches or vanishes; or he passes through the ground; or a second figure appears beside him; or his body morphs into another shape in mid-leap.

pc.expect: His clothing, the field and the background stay the same.
pc.fail: His clothing changes colour; or the field markings shift between frames; or the background rearranges.

note: Biomechanics scene: the boy is kept because his body is what carries the momentum. Athletic form, technique and how far he jumps are not judged; only the direction and order of the motion.
